headline_marked: First-ever [[BNP and Communist Party of China sign MoU]] to forge ties
headline: First-ever BNP and Communist Party of China sign MoU to forge ties
summary: The agreement was signed in Beijing at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse, marking the first such pact between the two political parties.
details: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the Communist Party of China (CPC) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen bilateral ties.
The signing ceremony took place at 8:45 am local time on Thursday at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse, a high-profile state diplomatic complex in Beijing.
Humayun Kabir, the BNP joint secretary general (international relations), signed the agreement on behalf of his party.
Liu Haixing, the CPC International Department Minister, signed the agreement on the Chinese side.
The BNP has stated that it will detail the specific terms and focus areas of the bilateral pact at a later media briefing.
The event was attended by several high-ranking officials, including Information Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon and Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen.
caption:
A historic first: The BNP and the Communist Party of China have signed their first-ever memorandum of understanding.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and the Communist Party of China (CPC) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to strengthen bilateral ties.

The signing ceremony took place at 8:45 am local time on Thursday at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse, a high-profile state diplomatic complex in Beijing.

Humayun Kabir, the BNP joint secretary general (international relations), signed the agreement on behalf of his party.

Liu Haixing, the CPC International Department Minister, signed the agreement on the Chinese side.

The BNP has stated that it will detail the specific terms and focus areas of the bilateral pact at a later media briefing.

The event was attended by several high-ranking officials, including Information Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon and Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen.

#BNP #China #CPC #BangladeshPolitics #Diplomacy #Beijing

Source: Somoy News, bdnews24.com, The Daily Star, Prothom Alo

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[invites Chinese companies to expand value chains]] in Bangladesh
headline: PM Tarique Rahman invites Chinese companies to expand value chains in Bangladesh
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met with Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the CCP, in Beijing to strengthen bilateral ties and investment.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a courtesy meeting with Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), at the Diaoyutai State Guest House in Beijing.

During the meeting, Liu Haixing congratulated the Prime Minister on assuming office and referenced the historical ties between the two nations, noting that a photo of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia's 2001 visit to China is preserved in the CCP museum.
The two leaders discussed expanding cooperation between the BNP and the CCP, specifically in areas such as media, think tanks, and improving the general public's quality of life.
Liu Haixing reaffirmed China's strong support for Bangladesh's sovereignty, security, and development, emphasizing the importance of mutual respect and cooperation.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed his desire for Chinese cooperation in various development projects, including the construction of the Bangladesh-China Friendship Hospital.
The meeting was attended by several high-level Bangladeshi ministers and advisors, including the Minister for Information and Broadcasting, and the Minister for Water Resources.
caption:
Bangladesh and China seek to deepen ties! PM Tarique Rahman meets CCP Minister Liu Haixing in Beijing to discuss investment and development.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman held a courtesy meeting with Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), at the Diaoyutai State Guest House in Beijing.

During the meeting, Liu Haixing congratulated the Prime Minister on assuming office and referenced the historical ties between the two nations, noting that a photo of former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia's 2001 visit to China is preserved in the CCP museum.

The two leaders discussed expanding cooperation between the BNP and the CCP, specifically in areas such as media, think tanks, and improving the general public's quality of life.

Liu Haixing reaffirmed China's strong support for Bangladesh's sovereignty, security, and development, emphasizing the importance of mutual respect and cooperation.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed his desire for Chinese cooperation in various development projects, including the construction of the Bangladesh-China Friendship Hospital.

The meeting was attended by several high-level Bangladeshi ministers and advisors, including the Minister for Information and Broadcasting, and the Minister for Water Resources.

#Bangladesh #China #Diplomacy #Investment #Beijing #TariqueRahman

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, Somoy News
